headline: Mandatory Orientation and Haida Heritage Permits
reservation: All visitors must attend a mandatory orientation session and obtain a specific entry permit before entering the park reserve. Given the high demand and limited daily quotas, reservations should be checked months in advance through the Parks Canada reservation system. Separate arrangements must be made for licensed tour operators if you are not using a private vessel.

days.title: Skidegate and the Cultural Gateway

stops.name: Haida Heritage Centre at Kay Llnagaay
stops.detail: Learn about the living culture and history of the Haida people before entering the protected wilderness.

stops.name: Balance Rock
stops.detail: Visit this glacial erratic on the beach outside Skidegate, a testament to the island's geological past.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local driving; island roads are paved but narrow in towns.
days.note: This day is on the 'mainland' of Graham Island; boat transit to the Park Reserve starts later.

days.title: Southern Reefs and Ancient Villages

stops.name: SGang Gwaay (Anthony Island)
stops.detail: View the iconic Haida mortuary poles at this UNESCO World Heritage site, accessible only by water.

stops.name: Burnaby Narrows
stops.detail: Witness the incredible intertidal diversity, known as one of the most vibrant marine displays in the world at low tide.

days.driving: Allow 4–6 hours of boat travel; transit times are highly dependent on sea states and tides.
days.note: Access to SGang Gwaay is strictly managed by Haida Watchmen; wait for invitation to land.

days.title: Hotsprings and Wilderness Coasts
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM via Zodiac or Floatplane

stops.name: Gandll K'in Gwaay.yaay (Hotspring Island)
stops.detail: Experience the natural thermal pools which have recently seen water levels return after seismic shifts.

stops.name: Windy Bay (Hlk'yah GawGa)
stops.detail: Walk through the old-growth forest to see the 'Legacy Pole' raised to commemorate the protection of the region.

days.driving: Allow 3–5 hours for water transit; conditions in Hecate Strait can be unpredictable.
days.note: Drought or seismic activity can affect the temperature and flow of the hot springs; check status locally.

intel.title: Marina Staging
intel.text: Long-term parking is available at Sandspit Airport or the Moresby Camp boat launch. Ensure no valuables are left in vehicles at these remote forest-service road trailheads.

intel.title: The Silent Archipelago
intel.text: There is no cellular service once you leave the northern towns of Sandspit or Queen Charlotte. Marine VHF radio and satellite messengers are the only forms of communication within the park.

intel.title: Marine and Road Supply
intel.text: The last reliable fuel for road vehicles is in Sandspit. Vessels must carry sufficient fuel for the entire journey, as no refueling stations exist within the park boundaries.

intel.title: Tidal Windows
intel.text: Many sites, particularly Burnaby Narrows, are only accessible or visible at specific low tide windows. Align your daily itinerary with the tide tables provided during your orientation.

intel.title: Marine-Only Interior
intel.text: Gwaii Haanas has no road access; the park begins south of Moresby Camp. All travel is via boat or floatplane, and visitors must be self-sufficient or on a guided tour.

plan.arrival: Fly into Sandspit (YZP), then take the airport shuttle or rental to your accommodation; buy all supplies in Skidegate or Queen Charlotte as options are extremely limited in Sandspit.
plan.vehicle: A 4WD vehicle is required for the logging roads to Moresby Camp; however, most visitors leave cars behind for boat-based expeditions.
plan.goldenHour: Views from the water near SGang Gwaay provide a hauntingly beautiful perspective of the poles against the Pacific sunset, weather permitting.
